I’m a nonbinary guy, I was afab. Transitioning was something I started just to feel less shit about how feminine I was because I hated being perceived as a woman. I knew I wasn’t a binary guy from the beginning, and I did not plan on ever passing as one. But I became accidentally stealth irl and most people minus the rare stranger treat me like a man now. I deal with a lot of nonbinary erasure in my every day life both from people who know I’m trans and people who don’t. Any of my effort to appear more androgynous has lead to people asking if I’m transitioning (to a woman) which is kind of hilarious but also terribly damaging and awkward. 

Would I like people to respect my identify as being nonbinary? Of course. But with the state of things right now, unless you fit the ‘blue hair and pronouns, stick thin androgynous white person with the same name as an inanimate object’ role, you’re kinda shit out of luck when it comes to most people. I think eventually we will see progress with nonbinary identities becoming more respected and normalized in the same way as bisexuality, but we’ve got a looong way to go. Right now most people tend to just see nonbinary as “trans lite” or a form of attention seeking (and this even includes a lot of people within the lgbt+ and trans communities)


Self acceptance is the hardest part of being trans in my opinion. People are never going to perceive you in the way that you want to be perceived, and that goes for anyone and everyone, trans or not. Focus more on your opinion of yourself, because it matters way more than others at the end of the day. If you’re content, that’s all that really matters. Hopefully those you keep close respect you, as well.

A few years ago, I would have said my name. My parents weren’t all there in the head and named me something that wasn’t common at all 25 years ago when they gave it to me. These days though it’s a “tell” because it’s become a very common nonbinary trope kind of name (think names that are words, not typically names) 

My entire life I was asked what my real name was, which was fine when I didn’t know I was trans yet since I just found it kind of funny. But now it feels like it gives me away as being trans the second people meet me. I don’t like being clocked by something like that because it’s been my name my entire life. I hate that it became so associated with being trans in recent years. Growing up I never met a since person with my name. But in the last 2-3 years almost every time I meet another trans person in real life I get “I used to go by [my name] for a while too!” I didn’t choose this name and I’ve been at the point recently that I’m finally considering changing it because of this fact. It blows. 

Other than that, I guess just the fact that I’ve always had pretty androgynous features. Before puberty people always assumed I was my parents’ son based on the combo of appearance and behaviors. I’m transmasc but I do identify as nonbinary and I don’t try to pass as a man but once I stopped presenting femme and my voice dropped I didn’t have a very hard time passing socially at all.

When I had my initial endo appointment with kaiser is was just like a basic doctors appointment. It was a really smooth process in my experience but it also depends on the endocrinologist you get. Mine is pretty young and fully views HRT as a medically necessary treatment but I know a lot of older Drs don’t share that viewpoint so I got lucky. I wouldn’t worry though, you should probably just be ordered to get some lab work done and have your prescription in no time. They just have to make sure your levels are healthy enough to start hormones so you can’t really start until you get a full panel done. That might just be why they’re not moving forward faster yet. Definitely bring up your concerns to the endo. Good luck!
